mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that may lead the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent FEDFUNDS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where RSAFS has increased for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where INDPRO has declined by more than 1% MoM, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is above 2% YoY, the real interest rate is negative, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the condition does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS has declined by more than 100,000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 10% YoY signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts consumer confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST has increased by more than 10% YoY, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% quarter-over-quarter and the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, the economy is likely in a stagflationary regime, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the condition does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.
